input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Clause 22.1 grants unlimited, unannounced audits and remote access to our systems, which is the playbook walk-away position. Cost allocation in 22.2 already matches the preferred 5% underpayment threshold and 22.2 bars direct system access, so 22.1 both breaches the rule and conflicts internally. We amended 22.1 to one audit per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where feasible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, with no direct or remote system access.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site via independent auditor, with no system access
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the unlimited, unannounced audit right and remote system access with our standard position: one audit per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where feasible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality and with no access to our systems. This also aligns 22.1 with the access restrictions already agreed in 22.2; we can accept 15 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's usage no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours and off-site wherever feasible, through an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement. Neither Vendor nor its auditor shall have direct or remote access to Customer's systems, and Customer may satisfy an audit by providing relevant records and reports.
